title: One round, every traded project audited
why: The biased verifier's reports are found out: who pays what, and who is told what.

title: One round, no audits
why: Without audits nobody learns the true qualities and no verifier is penalized.

title: The biased verifier reports the true qualities anyway
why: A verifier is judged on what it reports, not on what it measured.

title: A report that is off by less than the tolerance
why: An audited report 0.08 too high is not penalized (tolerance 0.1).

title: A report that is off by more than the tolerance
why: An audited report 0.15 too high costs the verifier one penalty per project.

title: A verifier understates quality
why: Is a report that is too low penalized like one that is too high?

title: A seller asks more than anyone bids
why: A project that does not trade is not audited, so its verifier cannot be penalized.

title: A buyer sends no orders
why: An empty order is allowed: the buyer trades nothing and earns nothing.

title: A seller does not act
why: A participant who does not act stops the whole run.

title: Two rounds, buyers see the audit record and use it
why: After round one the buyers bid less for the projects of the verifier that was caught.

title: Two rounds, the audit record is not shown
why: With the record hidden the same buyers cannot react to it.

title: Audits happen with probability one half
why: Only some traded projects are audited; the others stay unknown and unpenalized.

title: Buyers are credited on true quality
why: With settle_on = true a buyer's payoff uses the true quality, not the report.
